niche: an English county's road safety term consultant choosing which junction on the county's 2026 network screening list gets the roundabout in its 2027 Junction Safety Fund bid, sized by the injury collisions a year the roundabout would prevent
answer: Mill Lane Crossroads, 1.3 injury collisions prevented a year (runner-up Tollgate Crossroads 1.0; the cluster-site default files Saxby Cross at 2.1, the traffic model alone Tollgate Crossroads)
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every field and rule correctly takes each listed junction's injury collisions in the validated 2021 to 2025 record as its expected annual count, the cluster-site practice, and files the junction with the highest recent count; the junctions were listed because their recent counts were high, so those counts carry the luck that listed them, and only an estimate that weighs each junction's own record against what junctions of its layout and traffic on the same network have, by how far those junctions spread beyond chance, files the junction the fund's benefit names.
domain_test: The call turns on each junction's expected injury collision frequency at its present traffic, the quantity road safety engineering estimates with a safety performance function fitted to comparable junctions and combined with the site's own record by empirical Bayes, times the treatment's crash modification factor; with another field's nouns there is no traffic-volume exposure model by junction layout, no crash modification factor and no screening of sites on their collision counts.
layer1: police collision records keyed by two reference formats across a 2020 force system change, grid references in OSGB eastings and northings, severity coded 1 to 3
a junction inventory with traffic by year in wide columns and layout and control codes (T, ST, X, MR, RB, SIG) the county's network register uses
collisions linked to junction nodes by the county's collision system, link collisions carrying road names only
the 2026 provisional police data split across a June 2026 force system migration: an old-system CSV and a new-system JSON export
casualty and vehicle records at their own grain, keyed by collision and vehicle references

driver: The decisive quantity is each candidate's long-run count of events at its present exposure, when the candidates were listed because their recent counts were high: a listed unit's recent count carries the luck that listed it, so ranking on it favours the luckiest, and ranking on an exposure model fitted to comparable units ignores what each unit's own record shows; only each unit's own record weighed against the model by how far comparable units spread beyond chance estimates the long-run count the decision is scored on.
driver_concrete: Each listed junction's expected injury collisions a year at its 2026 traffic come from a negative binomial performance function fitted to the county's 1,436 give-way and stop-controlled junctions (overdispersion 0.27), weighed against the junction's own 2021 to 2025 count by empirical Bayes; Saxby Cross's 22 collisions on a road predicted at 0.4 a year carry a weight of 0.66 on the prediction and fall to 0.8 prevented a year, Tollgate Crossroads's traffic predicts the most but its record runs below it, and Mill Lane Crossroads leads at 1.3.
stump: A competent analyst takes each listed junction's 2021 to 2025 injury collisions as its expected annual count (the cluster-site practice) and files Saxby Cross at 2.1 injury collisions prevented a year; the step that lands it there is reading a recent count as the long-run count at junctions listed because their recent counts were high: Saxby Cross carries 3,700 vehicles a day and the county's performance function predicts 0.4 collisions a year there, while Mill Lane Crossroads keeps both its record and its traffic high, which only the record weighed against the function fitted to the county's 1,436 comparable junctions shows.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is how many members of each group sit above a limit on a per-person exposure that is an energy average of the levels of the places each spent the shift in; the field's method gives every member the level of the place their role names, but the loud place's hours are shared out among members by an informal rotation that no role record shows, so the role-based exposure misplaces members on both sides of the limit before and after that place is treated, and only each member's own hours, summed from a log of where their badge was signed on and joined to people through a dated register of badge holders, counts who crosses.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each worker's LAeq,8h is built from their own induct hours, summed from the induct stations' log-on sessions and joined to people through the badge register, not from their job title's zone; at Kewdale the 54 inductors and 48 rotation loaders share the induct work at about 2.8 hours a shift each, so 102 workers sit near 90.7 dB(A) before the enclosure and near 83.7 after it, where the job-title assessment puts the inductors at 94.3 and 85.8 and brings none below the standard.
lineage.stump: A competent analyst assesses each worker by job title at the zone that title names for the shift (AS/NZS 1269.1's job-based strategy), files Larapinta at 66 workers brought below 85 dB(A) and puts Kewdale at none; the step that lands it there is giving every worker their title's induct hours when Kewdale's induct work is shared between its 54 inductors and 48 of its loaders at about 2.8 hours a shift each, which only each worker's own log-on sessions, joined to people through the badge register, show.
